forecasts.question: Will the US government formally respond to Iran's September 23 written ceasefire roadmap — by accepting, publicly counter-proposing, or explicitly rejecting it — before EOD September 28, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 72h forecast. Iran FM Araghchi handed US envoy Witkoff a written 60-day ceasefire roadmap at the UNGA sidelines on September 23; SNSC Secretary Rezaei attached a 4-5 day US response deadline (~Sep 27-28) on September 24. Witkoff publicly called the talks 'promising, constructive'; Trump at UNGA said a deal is possible 'after the midterm elections.' The deadline creates a forcing function for a public US position — response is likely, though content (accept/counter/reject) is uncertain. p=0.55 reflects that the US is very likely to acknowledge the roadmap by the deadline but that a non-response or deliberate ambiguity remains plausible.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US official (President, Secretary of State, NSA, Witkoff, or Kushner) publicly states the US government's specific position on the September 23 Iran roadmap before EOD September 28 ET — whether accepting, counter-proposing, or explicitly rejecting it.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: White House press releases, US State Department official statements, or two independent TIER1 wire services (AP/Reuters/AFP) citing a named US official by name and specific reference to the Sep 23 roadmap.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: General statements about 'constructive talks' or 'considering options' without specific reference to the Sep 23 roadmap do NOT resolve YES. Trump social media posts alone without formal White House or State Dept confirmation do NOT resolve YES. The US must acknowledge the roadmap by name or describe its specific conditions.

indicators.name: Witkoff or Kushner public statement on Iran roadmap response
White House or State Dept press briefing citing Iran Sep 23 roadmap
Trump public statement explicitly accepting or rejecting Iran conditions

forecasts.question: Will there be zero confirmed CENTCOM airstrikes on Iranian sovereign territory during the period September 25 through October 1, 2026 (inclusive, 7 days)?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 7-day forecast. UNGA indirect talks (Sep 22-23) were the first confirmed Iran-US session since the June MOU collapsed; both sides characterized the session as constructive. Iran's Sep 27-28 ultimatum creates incentive for the US to avoid strikes that would collapse the diplomatic window before deadline. Against that: the conflict has continued with zero pause for 210 days; Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran at UNGA on Sep 23; IRGC struck a cargo vessel in Hormuz on Sep 23; the US has consistently responded kinetically to IRGC provocations. Base rate of a 7-day strike-free period in this conflict is low. p=0.35 reflects the diplomatic pause hypothesis.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if no CENTCOM press release, DoD daily brief, or two independent wire-service reports confirm any airstrike by US forces on Iranian sovereign territory during the window Sep 25-Oct 1, 2026. NO if any such strike is confirmed.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM Public Affairs, Pentagon press secretary, or two independent TIER1 sources (AP/Reuters/AFP/BBC) with on-record sourcing confirming a strike on Iranian territory.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: US strikes on Iranian proxies outside Iran (Houthi targets, IRGC-linked vessels in the Gulf, Iraqi militia targets) do NOT resolve NO — only confirmed strikes on Iranian sovereign territory. Naval engagements within the Strait of Hormuz do not resolve NO unless the strike occurs on Iranian-controlled land.

indicators.name: CENTCOM daily brief reports no new strikes on Iranian territory
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES per day with no strike

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: Major downward revision: 0.22→0.05. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 commercial transit on September 20 (vs 85/day pre-war baseline); The National (Sep 21) confirmed traffic remains 'thin'; a cargo vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait on September 23 with two casualties. Iran SNSC Secretary Rezaei set a Sep 27-28 deadline for US to accept 7 conditions before the Strait reopens; even Rezaei's own optimistic scenario ('Hormuz can reopen in 7 days once US accepts') would not achieve a 30/day 7-day rolling average by October 3. The DA flagged a brief Sep 17-19 spike to ~32/day on some trackers; this does not constitute resolution since the criterion is a 7-day rolling average, not a single-day or 3-day spike — the surrounding baseline of 1-11/day means the 7-day rolling average never crossed 30. Judge sets p=0.05 (schema floor). The threshold is mathematically unreachable given 8 days to horizon and 1 transit/day.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any AIS-based ship-tracking source (IMF PortWatch, Straits.live, MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: AIS-based tracker + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit. If trackers diverge by >20%, flag AMBIGUOUS. A brief 1-3 day spike above 30 does NOT satisfy the 7-day rolling average criterion; sustained ≥30/day averaged over 7 consecutive days is required.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES — current opposite trend (attacks Sep 21, Sep 23)

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: Update: 0.42→0.33. Four of five polls published after candidate lists closed show Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party leading Likud: Channel 12 (Sep 23, Haaretz) gives Yashar 23 seats vs Likud 20; an earlier Channel 12 survey placed Yashar at 25 seats vs Likud 21; the Israel Policy Forum 120 Project tracker consistently places Yashar first. One i24NEWS/Direct Polls outlier shows Likud at 27 seats ahead of Yashar at 22. Jerusalem Post (Sep 23): 'Eisenkot leads most surveys, Likud gains in one.' Netanyahu's corruption trial continues through the campaign. Analyst proposed 0.28 and DA proposed 0.35; Judge calibrates at 0.33, reflecting the polling consensus while preserving uncertainty 32 days before election.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

forecasts.question: Will a formal bilateral US-Iran ceasefire agreement take effect before EOD November 15, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 51-day forecast. UNGA indirect session (Sep 22-23) was the first confirmed US-Iran meeting since the June MOU collapsed in July. Iran's written 60-day roadmap was handed to Witkoff on Sep 23 — the first formal written Iranian proposal since the MOU. Key structural obstacle: Trump at UNGA said a deal is possible 'after the midterm elections' (US midterms Nov 3), implying a 5-6 week delay before meaningful US movement. If Trump wins midterms and seeks a foreign-policy deal, the Nov 3-15 window is narrow but plausible. Against: Iran's 7 conditions include US blockade-lifting as a precondition; Trump has publicly ruled this out before 'sufficient goodwill.' p=0.20 reflects approximately 30% probability of a post-midterm deal, discounted by probability Trump prioritizes Iran and by Iran's conditions gap.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both the US and Iranian governments have mutually announced a ceasefire in simultaneous or coordinated public statements, with the ceasefire taking effect before EOD November 15 ET.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: White House + Iranian MFA or SNSC (both must publish), or three major wire services (AP/Reuters/AFP) citing both governments in the same news cycle.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral pauses or informal lulls without joint announcement do not count. A US-only declaration without Iranian confirmation does not count. Both governments must have announced a commitment, not merely transmitted messages through intermediaries.

indicators.name: US formally accepts or counter-proposes on Iran's Sep 23 roadmap (F2 resolution)
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES if accepted; -5pp if rejected

Sustained kinetic pause (F3) — both sides hold fire for 7 days

forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. President Pezeshkian stated on Sep 1 that Iran would 'reciprocate' if the US returned to the June MOU — a conditional formulation that does not meet the resolution criterion of an unconditional MFA announcement of readiness. The forecast was written Sep 3 after these conditional statements with p=0.12, confirming the authors did not count conditional statements as resolution. The IRGC attacked US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq on Sep 2 concurrent with the diplomatic language. No standalone unconditional MFA announcement appeared before Sep 6. First confirmed indirect session: Sep 22-23 at UNGA, sixteen days past the horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, SNSC, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Araghchi or SNSC public statement committing to talks
Oman or Qatar mediator readout citing named Iranian acceptance

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated, senior officials, named principals) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. Judge ruling: DA proposed RESOLVED-YES citing Al Jazeera Aug 9 'US and Iran are talking past each other in indirect negotiations'; Analyst proposed RESOLVED-NO. Judge accepts Analyst's position. The confirmed session with named principals (Witkoff/Kushner, Araghchi, Qatari mediators, ~3 hours) occurred September 22-23, five days past the Sep 17 horizon. The Sep 16 written Iranian proposal transmitted via Qatari intermediaries in Doha was a document transfer, not a bilateral negotiating session. The resolution criteria explicitly excluded 'mere message relay' — the Aug 9 Al Jazeera report of contacts 'talking past each other' falls within the ambiguity_rule ('Message relay through intermediaries without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO'). No session with named principals was convened before Sep 17.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session (not mere message relay) between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official mediator readout.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Message relay through intermediaries without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump assertions of 'semi-negotiating' without Iranian or mediator confirmation of a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Oman/Qatar/Pakistan mediator readout of a convened session
Iran MFA confirms re-engagement or talks readiness
US-Iran bilateral halt in strikes for 72h+ (precondition)

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RETIRE-OBE. The Knesset dissolved July 17 at its natural four-year term end — the first government to complete a full term since 1988. The question asked whether the coalition would 'lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early' — neither occurred. The coalition served a full term; dissolution on July 17 was on schedule, not early. The October 27 election was set by the outgoing coalition as a caretaker government action. The path to YES (early dissolution) closed on July 17. Both Analyst and DA agree on OBE retirement. F7 retires as superseded by the natural timeline event.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.expected_effect: Knesset dissolved naturally Jul 17; this path is permanently closed
